chapter.text: The train pulled in after hours of waiting. Mara saw Leo step onto the platform. “You came back,” she said, letting out a breath. Later she found his name on the unsigned note. “You came back,” she said, keeping the paper hidden. At dawn she saw his packed bag beside the door. “You came back,” she said, looking past him.

chapter.text: Mara held up the brass key. “Nia, check the hall,” she said. Nia raised her torch. “No one is there.” Leo frowned at the lock. “Then why did the handle move?” The three of them listened. “It could be the wind,” Mara said. Nia lowered the torch. “There isn't any wind.” Leo put his hand on the door. “Give me a moment.”

chapter.text: The guard's steps sounded above them. “Stay behind me,” Leo whispered. Nia put out her torch. “Is he coming down?” she whispered. “I don't think so,” Mara whispered. The steps faded along the upper passage. The room returned to its ordinary hush. Mara opened the map and flattened a torn corner with her palm.

chapter.text: Leo pushed the door and its hinge fell off. “Wonderful,” he said dryly. Nia glanced at the empty corridor. “That is one way in.” Mara looked at the broken hinge but did not smile. The sign beside them read “STAFF ONLY”.

chapter.text: The following morning Nia reached the station first. The ticket office window bore a faded sign: “CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE”. She remembered the previous night's key. Mara arrived with a notebook. “Did you find anything?” she asked. Leo came in behind her. “Only a drawing of the old door.” Nia turned to him. “Show me.” The three of them bent over the page. A child had drawn a small star beside the hinge. Nia smiled at the careless sketch. 😊
